nodes.text: If the insured disputes the amount of loss stated in the carrier estimate, the dispute must be submitted for resolution under the valuation-dispute procedure.

Complete supplied procedure inventory for valuation disputes: intake trigger, adjuster review, estimate comparison, communication, resolution record. No escalation owner, escalation destination, or escalation deadline is defined in the supplied procedure.
The adjuster compares the two estimates and discusses the difference with the insured. The adjuster records the discussion and the final disposition.
Inspected components: actor = missing; route = missing; deadline = missing. The supplied procedure contains no supervisor queue, appraisal referral, dispute mailbox, or time limit.
When a covered property loss remains disputed after the insured receives the written valuation, the claim enters the valuation dispute state.

The supplied Claims Resolution Guide v4 is the complete valuation-dispute workflow for Homeowners claims in Ohio. It includes intake, estimate review, communications, and closure; escalation owner, escalation route, and escalation time limit are not specified.
The assigned adjuster attempts to reconcile the estimates and closes the dispute when the claim record contains a disposition note.

The component inventory found no named escalation actor, no receiving queue or referral route, and no deadline measured from the dispute trigger. The phrase ‘management review as needed’ appears only in an index and has no owner or handoff rule.
